$why: THE SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for who READS each answer the creator gives us.
A creator answers nine questions during the scan and on confirm. Every answer
is validated, sanitized and written to brand_voices.pre_script_brief. Four of
them are then read by nothing at all: the script generator never learns whether
it is writing for a doctor, a SaaS founder or a hobbyist, and the captured
product it could name is never offered to it.
That is a worse state than not asking. A question spends the creator's
attention and buys a promise — implicit but unmistakable — that the answer
changes what they get. An answer nothing reads breaks that promise silently,
and silence is why it survived: every individual PR that added a question was
correct, tested, and shipped green.
So the rule is mechanical rather than remembered: every key in
BRIEF_STORED_KEYS declares its readers HERE, and check_brief_consumers.mjs
fails the build when this file and the repository disagree.
WHY UNWIRED KEYS ARE DECLARED RATHER THAN TOLERATED. A guard that simply
demanded a reader for every key could not land until every key had one — so it
would land last, after the next asked-and-discarded fact had already been
added, which is precisely the failure it exists to prevent. Instead the debt is
written down: `readBy: []` plus an `unwiredReason` naming what is missing.
THE EXEMPTION EXPIRES BY ITSELF. The guard verifies both directions — a key
declared unwired must have NO reader in supabase/functions. The moment someone
wires one up, this file is wrong and the build says so. An exemption that
quietly stays true after it stops being true is how the original bug got in.
$fields: readBy      — paths under supabase/functions that must contain the key.
Every path must exist AND mention the key; a stale entry fails.
unwiredReason — required when readBy is empty. Says what is missing, not that
nothing is missing. Delete it in the same PR that adds a reader.

productEvidence.unwiredReason: The captured product — pixels and a section map — never reaches the prompt, so '[SHOW: the product]' still has nothing to point at and the model is free to invent product details.

alsoWantsToMake.unwiredReason: Asked on confirm and read by nothing. Either give it a consumer or stop asking it.
